SCD is a genetic disorder characterized by hemolytic anemia and vaso-occlusive complications; the pathophysiology of SCD is complex and incompletely understood, and is the focus of ongoing research efforts; and the treatment landscape is evolving as new therapies are introduced and as current therapies are evaluated in multi-center trials.

(1) SCD was once a fatal disease of infancy and early childhood; (2) supportive and preventive care has improved survival to over 95% in developed countries, and (3) the NHLBI now recommends that HU therapy be offered to all SCD patients beginning at 9 y of age, and that HU is an acceptable alternative to chronic transfusion therapy for stroke prevention.
